narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated an 82% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high-risk prediction, and it was treated as sufficient reason to reject your application. The strongest driver was your third-year class-standing decile of 1, far below the average of about 6 among students who were accepted; this was the most influential factor and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year standing was the second most important factor, also at a decile of 1 versus an accepted-student average of about 6, and it added further risk. Your LSAT score of 36, slightly below the accepted-student average of roughly 37, was the third most important factor; in this case it leaned toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the academic-standing signals. Gender and race were not used in the prediction. To improve your chances, ask admissions what would strengthen a future application, focus on raising or explaining your academic record, consider whether retaking the LSAT is realistic, and build evidence of bar-exam readiness through legal work, structured study, or a post-graduate program before reapplying.
